selected_hotel.name: Aegean Bliss Resort, Swiss Alps, Switzerland

experiences.name: Skiing on Jungfrau Region Slopes
experiences.description: Enjoy world-class skiing across the interconnected slopes of Grindelwald, Wengen, and Mürren. The Jungfrau Ski Region offers over 200km of groomed runs suitable for all skill levels, making it perfect for families with mixed abilities. Rent equipment on-site and take advantage of ski school lessons for younger children.

experiences.name: Glacier Snowshoeing Adventure
experiences.description: Embark on a guided family snowshoeing tour across the Aletsch Glacier, the largest glacier in the Alps. A certified mountain guide leads the way through stunning frozen landscapes, teaching kids about glaciology and alpine ecosystems. Gear is provided and no prior experience is needed, making it ideal for families.

experiences.name: Tobogganing on the Fläsch Run
experiences.description: Experience one of Switzerland's most thrilling natural toboggan runs stretching over 7km from Preda down to Bergün. Families can ride the train back up and repeat the run multiple times throughout the day. This iconic winter activity is beloved by locals and visitors alike and is perfectly safe for children aged 5 and up.

experiences.name: Swiss Alpine Cheese and Fondue Cultural Experience
experiences.description: Visit a traditional alpine dairy farm in Gruyères to see authentic Swiss cheese being made, followed by a hands-on fondue cooking class for the whole family. Learn about centuries-old Swiss culinary traditions while enjoying a hearty meal together. This cultural and gastronomic experience gives deep insight into Swiss mountain heritage.

experiences.name: Jungfraujoch Top of Europe Train Excursion
experiences.description: Ride the iconic cogwheel railway to Jungfraujoch at 3,454 meters, the highest railway station in Europe. Explore the Ice Palace carved inside the glacier, walk on the snow plateau, and take in breathtaking panoramic views of the Bernese Alps. The visitor center offers interactive exhibits about alpine science that children find fascinating.

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Swiss Alps, Switzerland
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

hotel.name: Aegean Bliss Resort, Swiss Alps, Switzerland

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled - flight arrives at 22:30
day_by_day.afternoon: No activities scheduled - in transit
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Zurich or Geneva Airport at 22:30 on flight UA. Take the most budget-friendly train or shuttle transfer toward the Swiss Alps region. Check into Aegean Bliss Resort, collect your room key, and settle in. Do a quick unpack and review your week's plan. Get to bed early to recover from travel.

meals.breakfast: On the plane or at airport
meals.lunch: On the plane or at airport
meals.dinner: Grab a quick bite at the airport before departure or pick up a sandwich/snack at a convenience store or train station kiosk (CHF 5–10) on the way to the resort

day_by_day.notes: Keep all receipts for budget tracking. Purchase a Swiss Travel Pass or regional ski area transport pass at the airport if planning to use public transport heavily — it can save significant money over the week. Confirm resort check-in procedures in advance since arrival is late at night. Pack light snacks for the journey.

day_by_day.morning: Sleep in and recover from jet lag. Enjoy a leisurely breakfast at the resort or a nearby local bakery. After breakfast, take a short orientation walk around the village to get your bearings — identify the ski rental shops, supermarkets, and free or low-cost attractions nearby. Visit the local tourist information office to pick up free maps and ask about any discounted lift passes or family ski packages available this week.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to the nearest beginner or intermediate ski slope for a half-day introductory ski session. Rent ski equipment from a local rental shop (budget around CHF 30–45/person for full gear rental). Look for group ski lessons which are much cheaper than private instruction (CHF 30–50/person for a group lesson). Many Swiss resorts offer family ski packages — ask at the ski school desk. Spend 2–3 hours on the bunny slopes or easy green runs to get comfortable.
day_by_day.evening: Return ski gear and head back to the resort to warm up with hot chocolate. Explore the village on foot in the early evening — many Swiss alpine villages have charming pedestrian zones with free ice skating rinks or winter markets in February. Enjoy a relaxed dinner at a budget-friendly local restaurant or self-catering at the resort.

meals.breakfast: Local bakery or resort breakfast — try a croissant and coffee (CHF 8–12). Alternatively, buy bread, cheese, and yogurt from a Migros or Coop supermarket for a self-prepared budget breakfast (CHF 5–8)
meals.lunch: Pack a sandwich or buy from a ski slope snack bar — look for the daily soup special which is usually CHF 8–12. Avoid sit-down mountain restaurants which can be very expensive.
meals.dinner: Budget restaurant in the village — look for a Fondue Stübli or local gasthaus offering a set menu (CHF 20–30/person). Alternatively, cook a simple pasta meal if your accommodation has kitchen access (CHF 5–10/person)

day_by_day.notes: February in the Swiss Alps typically means cold temperatures (-5°C to -15°C at altitude) and good snow conditions. Dress in warm layers. Sunscreen is essential even in winter — UV rays are strong at altitude. Check if the resort or local ski area offers a 'beginner package' combining lift pass, rental, and lesson at a discounted rate.

day_by_day.morning: Early start — purchase a full-day ski lift pass (look for multi-day passes which offer better value; a 6-day pass is often 20–30% cheaper per day than a single-day pass). Head to the ski area by 9:00 AM to beat crowds on the lifts. Spend the morning skiing blue (easy) and red (intermediate) runs. Take advantage of the quiet morning slopes before the midday rush.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue skiing after a quick and affordable mountain lunch. In the mid-afternoon (around 3:00–3:30 PM), the slopes get icy and more crowded — a good time to take a break. Try snowshoeing as a free or very low-cost alternative activity — many resorts have marked snowshoe trails accessible without a lift pass. Snowshoe rental is typically CHF 15–20/day. This is a great family-friendly activity with stunning alpine scenery.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort by 5:00 PM. Warm up with Glühwein (mulled wine) or hot chocolate at a village bar — many offer happy hour deals. Visit the resort's indoor facilities if available (sauna, pool) — check if these are included in your accommodation. Prepare a budget home-cooked dinner or visit a local pizzeria.

meals.breakfast: Self-prepared at resort — oatmeal, fruit, and coffee purchased from Migros/Coop supermarket (CHF 4–6/person)
meals.lunch: On-mountain — bring a packed lunch (sandwiches, energy bars, thermos of hot soup) to save CHF 20–30 compared to mountain restaurant prices. Find a sunny terrace to eat your packed lunch with a view.
meals.dinner: Local pizzeria or kebab shop in the village (CHF 15–22/person). Many Swiss alpine villages have surprisingly affordable pizza restaurants that are popular with budget travelers and ski workers.

day_by_day.notes: Multi-day ski passes offer the best value — if you plan to ski 4+ days, buy a 5 or 6-day pass upfront. Some resorts offer family discounts where children under 9 ski free when parents purchase adult passes. Always check the resort's website or tourist office for current promotions.

day_by_day.morning: Take a rest day from skiing to explore the wider area and save on lift pass costs. After breakfast, take a scenic train or local bus ride through the alpine valley — Swiss public transport is punctual and offers stunning views. Visit a nearby alpine village on foot — many have free-to-visit historic churches, village squares, and viewpoints. If near Grindelwald, Zermatt, or Interlaken, explore the town center which is free.
day_by_day.afternoon: Enjoy a family-friendly winter activity: try tobogganing (sledding) which is one of the most affordable and fun winter activities in Switzerland. Many resorts have dedicated toboggan runs with sled rental for CHF 10–15/person. Alternatively, visit a free or low-cost natural ice skating rink if available in the village. Spend 2–3 hours sledding and playing in the snow — great for families with children.
day_by_day.evening: Warm up at the resort. Visit a local supermarket (Migros or Coop — Switzerland's most affordable chains) to stock up on groceries for self-catering meals. Cook a hearty Swiss-inspired dinner at the resort: try making Rösti (Swiss potato dish) with eggs and cheese — simple, filling, and budget-friendly. Spend the evening playing board games or cards as a family.

meals.breakfast: Resort breakfast or self-prepared — Swiss muesli with milk and fresh fruit (CHF 4–5/person from supermarket)
meals.lunch: Picnic-style lunch at a scenic viewpoint or village bench — buy fresh bread, local cheese (Gruyère or Emmental), cold cuts, and fruit from a supermarket (CHF 8–12/person). This is a very Swiss way to eat lunch!
meals.dinner: Self-catered at resort — homemade Rösti with fried eggs, cheese, and a green salad (CHF 6–8/person in ingredients). Buy a bottle of affordable Swiss wine from the supermarket (CHF 8–15) to enjoy with dinner.

day_by_day.notes: This rest day is important for budget management and physical recovery. Skiing every day is exhausting and expensive. Use this day to explore the free cultural and natural attractions of the Alps. Check the local tourist office for free events, markets, or guided walks happening this week.

day_by_day.morning: Back on the slopes for another full ski day. Focus on improving skills — try more challenging red or black runs if confidence has grown. Consider a morning group ski lesson to advance technique (CHF 30–50 for a 2-hour group lesson). Many ski schools offer a midweek discount on lessons. Head out early (8:30–9:00 AM) to enjoy freshly groomed pistes.
day_by_day.afternoon: After lunch, try a different area of the ski resort — use the lift system to explore new runs and terrain. If traveling with children, look for dedicated family ski areas with magic carpet lifts and fun features. In late afternoon, try cross-country skiing (Langlauf) as an alternative — it uses different muscles and is often cheaper than downhill (trail pass CHF 5–15, rental CHF 20–25).
day_by_day.evening: Après-ski at a budget-friendly mountain bar — enjoy one drink and soak up the atmosphere without overspending. Many bars have live music or DJ sets on weekday evenings in February. Head back to the resort for dinner. Tonight, splurge slightly on a traditional Swiss fondue experience — either at a restaurant or buy a fondue set and ingredients from the supermarket to make it yourself (CHF 15–20 for ingredients vs CHF 35–50 at a restaurant).

meals.breakfast: Early self-prepared breakfast — toast, peanut butter, banana, and coffee (CHF 3–5/person)
meals.lunch: Packed lunch on the mountain — thermos of hot soup, sandwiches, chocolate bar, and fruit. Eat at a mountain hut terrace without purchasing (some huts allow this, others require a purchase — buy a hot drink if so, CHF 4–6).
meals.dinner: DIY Swiss cheese fondue at the resort — buy a fondue kit, Gruyère and Emmental cheese, white wine, bread, and vegetables from Migros/Coop (CHF 15–20/person). This is a memorable, fun, and surprisingly affordable Swiss experience when done at home.

day_by_day.notes: Fondue tip: Traditional Swiss fondue recipe requires Gruyère, Emmental, a splash of kirsch (cherry brandy), white wine, and a garlic-rubbed pot. Most Swiss supermarkets sell pre-mixed fondue cheese blends for convenience. Make sure your accommodation has a fondue set — if not, they are inexpensive to buy or sometimes available to borrow from reception.

day_by_day.morning: Adventure day — try a new winter sport! Look into ice climbing introductory sessions (some resorts offer these for CHF 40–60 with equipment included), or try ski touring (ski mountaineering) with a guided group tour. Alternatively, visit a local alpine sports center for indoor climbing or other winter activities. If budget is tight, stick to free activities: build a snowman, have a snowball fight, or hike a marked winter walking trail (many are free and well-maintained).
day_by_day.afternoon: Take a scenic cable car or gondola ride to a high-altitude viewpoint — many Swiss resorts have a summit viewing platform accessible by gondola. The views of the Alps in February are spectacular. Check if your ski lift pass covers the gondola — if so, this is free! Visit a mountain restaurant at the top for a hot drink and enjoy the panoramic views. Spend 1–2 hours at the summit before descending.
day_by_day.evening: Final big ski dinner night — treat the family to a sit-down meal at a mid-range local restaurant. Look for a set menu (Tagesmenü) which typically includes starter, main course, and sometimes dessert at a fixed price (CHF 25–35/person) — much better value than ordering à la carte. Try traditional Swiss dishes: Zürcher Geschnetzeltes (veal in cream sauce), Älplermagronen (alpine macaroni), or Bündner Nusstorte (walnut tart) for dessert.

meals.breakfast: Treat yourself to a café breakfast today — visit a local bakery for fresh-baked bread, butter, jam, and a proper Swiss coffee (CHF 10–15/person). Well-deserved after a great week!
meals.lunch: Mountain summit café — hot chocolate, a slice of apple strudel or cake (CHF 8–15/person). Keep it light as dinner will be a bigger meal.
meals.dinner: Local Swiss restaurant set menu (Tagesmenü) — CHF 25–35/person including a drink. Ask for tap water (Leitungswasser) instead of bottled water to save CHF 4–6 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Always ask for tap water at Swiss restaurants — it is perfectly safe and free or very cheap. Ordering bottled water adds unnecessary cost. Tipping in Switzerland is appreciated but not obligatory — rounding up the bill or leaving 5–10% is sufficient and customary.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in the Swiss Alps! Wake up early and take one last walk or snowshoe through the alpine landscape to soak in the scenery. If energy and budget allow, do a short final ski session (2–3 hours) to make the most of any remaining lift pass validity. Return rental equipment by the agreed time to avoid extra charges. Take photos and enjoy the mountain air one last time.
day_by_day.afternoon: Check out of Aegean Bliss Resort — confirm checkout time in advance. Store luggage with the concierge if needed. Use the afternoon to do any last-minute souvenir shopping — budget-friendly Swiss souvenirs include: Ricola herbal sweets (CHF 3–5), Swiss chocolate bars from the supermarket (CHF 2–4 each, much cheaper than airport prices), small Edelweiss trinkets, or a postcard. Buy chocolates and souvenirs at Migros or Coop rather than tourist shops to save 30–50%.
day_by_day.evening: Head to the airport or train station for your onward journey. Allow plenty of travel time — Swiss trains are reliable but alpine routes can take 2–3 hours to reach major airports. Have a final Swiss meal at a train station restaurant or airport — try a Brezel (pretzel) and a Swiss beer for a classic farewell snack. Board your flight home with wonderful alpine memories!

meals.breakfast: Quick self-prepared breakfast using remaining groceries — finish up any leftover bread, cheese, fruit, and yogurt to avoid waste (CHF 0–3/person)
meals.lunch: Light lunch at a village café or train station — soup of the day and bread roll (CHF 10–15/person)
meals.dinner: Airport or train station meal — look for a Migros To Go or Coop To Go outlet at the station for affordable sandwiches, salads, and drinks (CHF 10–15/person). Much cheaper than sit-down airport restaurants.

day_by_day.notes: Budget summary tips for the week: 1) Always buy groceries at Migros or Coop for self-catered meals. 2) Multi-day ski passes save 20–30% vs daily passes. 3) Group ski lessons vs private save 60–70%. 4) Pack your own mountain lunch daily to save CHF 20–30/day. 5) Use Swiss public transport with a regional pass for free or discounted travel. 6) Ask at the tourist office for free events and activities daily. Estimated total budget for 7 days (excluding flights and accommodation): CHF 600–900/person depending on skiing days and dining choices.

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled — late night arrival at 22:30 via Flight UA. Transfer from airport to Aegean Bliss Resort. Check-in, unpack, and settle into your accommodations.
day_by_day.afternoon: No activities scheduled due to late arrival.
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at 22:30. Quick late-night snack at the resort's 24-hour lounge or in-room dining. Rest and prepare for the week ahead. Review ski rental and lift pass options available at the resort front desk.

meals.breakfast: Not applicable — travel day
meals.lunch: Not applicable — travel day
meals.dinner: Late-night in-room dining or resort lounge snack upon arrival (CHF 20–35). Try a light Swiss-style sandwich or soup to wind down.

day_by_day.notes: Arrival is late at night, so no sightseeing or activities are planned. Confirm ski equipment rental bookings for Day 2 at check-in. Exchange currency or confirm card acceptance at the resort. Get a good night's rest to acclimatize to the alpine altitude.

day_by_day.morning: Leisurely breakfast at the resort to recover from travel. After breakfast, head to the resort ski rental shop to pick up equipment and purchase lift passes. Take a gentle orientation ski run on beginner-to-intermediate slopes near the resort to get your ski legs back. Ideal for families to assess skill levels before tackling larger runs.
day_by_day.afternoon: Begin the Skiing on Jungfrau Region Slopes experience — enjoy world-class skiing across the interconnected slopes of Grindelwald, Wengen, and Mürren. Families can split between beginner zones and intermediate blue runs. Take the gondola up for panoramic alpine views and enjoy a mid-afternoon hot chocolate break at a mountain hut.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort by 17:00. Warm up with a relaxing soak if the resort has a spa or hot tub. Enjoy a classic Swiss dinner at a nearby mid-range restaurant in the village.

meals.breakfast: Buffet breakfast at Aegean Bliss Resort (included or CHF 18–28). Enjoy eggs, pastries, Swiss muesli, and fresh fruit.
meals.lunch: Mountain restaurant lunch on the slopes — try Rösti (Swiss potato cake) with a side salad and warm soup (CHF 25–40 per person).
meals.dinner: Dinner at a local alpine restaurant in the village — order traditional Zürcher Geschnetzeltes (veal in cream sauce) or cheese fondue for the family (CHF 35–55 per person).

day_by_day.notes: Rent ski equipment early in the morning to avoid queues. Purchase multi-day Jungfrau ski passes for better value if skiing on multiple days. Ensure children have properly fitted helmets. Check current slope conditions and weather forecast before heading out.

day_by_day.morning: After breakfast, embark on the Jungfraujoch Top of Europe Train Excursion. Board the iconic cogwheel railway from Grindelwald or Kleine Scheidegg up to Jungfraujoch at 3,454 meters — the highest railway station in Europe. Marvel at breathtaking glacier views, visit the Ice Palace, and explore the Sphinx Observatory.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue exploring Jungfraujoch — enjoy the snow activities on the plateau including short snowshoe walks, zip lines, and snow tubing available at the summit. Visit the Alpine Sensation exhibition inside the tunnel. Begin descent by 15:00 to avoid cold afternoon winds at altitude.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort by 17:30. Freshen up and enjoy a relaxed family dinner at the resort restaurant or a nearby fondue house in the village.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the resort before an early departure (CHF 18–28 or included). Eat heartily before the high-altitude excursion.
meals.lunch: Lunch at the Crystal Restaurant at Jungfraujoch — self-service alpine buffet with hot dishes, soups, and Swiss specialties (CHF 30–45 per person).
meals.dinner: Traditional Swiss cheese fondue dinner at a village fondue restaurant — a must-do family experience (CHF 30–50 per person including bread and salad).

day_by_day.notes: Book Jungfraujoch train tickets in advance online to secure your preferred departure time and avoid sold-out slots. The excursion costs approximately CHF 145–210 per adult (discounts for children and Swiss Travel Pass holders). Dress in warm layers — temperatures at the summit can be -15°C or below. The train journey itself takes about 2 hours each way and is a spectacular experience.

day_by_day.morning: After breakfast, head out for the Glacier Snowshoeing Adventure — a guided family snowshoeing tour across the Aletsch Glacier, the largest glacier in the Alps. The guide will provide all necessary equipment and safety briefing. Suitable for families with children aged 6 and above. Enjoy stunning glacier scenery and learn about the glacier's geology.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the snowshoeing tour through the afternoon or wrap up by 13:00 and enjoy free time at a nearby winter sports area. Families can try ice skating at a local outdoor rink or simply explore the snowy alpine village on foot. Visit local artisan shops for Swiss souvenirs.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort for a relaxing evening. Enjoy the resort facilities — spa, pool, or games room for the kids. Optional family movie night in the room.

meals.breakfast: Hearty resort breakfast to fuel the snowshoeing adventure (CHF 18–28 or included). Opt for protein-rich options like eggs and cheese.
meals.lunch: Packed lunch provided by the snowshoeing tour guide or a quick bite at a mountain café — sandwiches, soup, and hot drinks (CHF 15–25 per person).
meals.dinner: Dinner at a mid-range Swiss brasserie in the village — try Raclette (melted cheese over potatoes) or Alpine pasta dishes (CHF 30–45 per person).

day_by_day.notes: Book the Glacier Snowshoeing Adventure in advance as guided tours fill up quickly in peak season. Wear waterproof boots and warm layers. Snowshoes and poles are typically provided by the guide. The Aletsch Glacier is a UNESCO World Heritage Site — follow all guide instructions to stay on safe paths. This is a wonderful educational experience for children.

day_by_day.morning: After breakfast, return to the Jungfrau Region Slopes for a second full day of skiing. Now more familiar with the area, tackle more challenging red runs or explore different sectors of the interconnected ski area. Families can split up with stronger skiers exploring Mürren's steep terrain while beginners continue on Grindelwald's gentler slopes.
day_by_day.afternoon: Mid-afternoon ski break — stop at a classic Swiss mountain hut (Bergrestaurant) for lunch and warm drinks. Continue skiing until 16:00, then head to the Tobogganing on the Fläsch Run experience — experience one of Switzerland's most thrilling natural toboggan runs stretching over 7km from Preda. An exhilarating family-friendly activity to end the ski day.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort tired and exhilarated. Enjoy a relaxing hot shower or spa session. Celebrate a great day on the slopes with a special family dinner at a slightly elevated mid-range restaurant.

meals.breakfast: Resort breakfast (CHF 18–28 or included). Load up on carbohydrates for an active skiing day.
meals.lunch: Lunch at a Bergrestaurant on the slopes — Bratwurst with bread, Rösti, or alpine soup (CHF 20–35 per person).
meals.dinner: Celebratory dinner at a well-regarded alpine restaurant — try Swiss Wiener Schnitzel, beef fondue, or seasonal game dishes (CHF 40–60 per person).

day_by_day.notes: The Fläsch toboggan run is a separate excursion from the ski area — check transport logistics and opening times in advance. Toboggan sleds can be rented on-site for CHF 10–15. The run is suitable for children over 6 with adult supervision. Wear helmets and gloves. Consider booking a ski instructor for children on Day 5 to help them progress to more challenging runs.

day_by_day.morning: After breakfast, depart for the Swiss Alpine Cheese and Fondue Cultural Experience. Travel to a traditional alpine dairy farm in Gruyères to see authentic Swiss cheese being made. Watch cheesemakers work with traditional copper cauldrons, learn about the centuries-old Gruyère cheese-making process, and sample fresh cheeses.
day_by_day.afternoon: Enjoy an immersive fondue lunch at the farm as part of the cultural experience. After lunch, explore the medieval village of Gruyères — visit Gruyères Castle, stroll the cobblestone streets, and browse local artisan shops for Swiss chocolate, cheese, and souvenirs. Return to the resort by 17:30.
day_by_day.evening: Final evening at the resort — enjoy a farewell family dinner at the resort's main restaurant. Let the kids choose their favorite Swiss dish from the week. After dinner, pack bags and prepare for departure the following morning.

meals.breakfast: Resort breakfast before departure for Gruyères (CHF 18–28 or included).
meals.lunch: Traditional cheese fondue lunch at the alpine dairy farm in Gruyères — included or partially included in the cultural experience package (CHF 35–55 per person).
meals.dinner: Farewell dinner at Aegean Bliss Resort restaurant — order family favorites from the week including Rösti, fondue, or Raclette (CHF 35–55 per person).

day_by_day.notes: Gruyères is approximately 1.5–2 hours from the Jungfrau region by train or car — plan transport in advance. The Swiss Alpine Cheese and Fondue Cultural Experience is highly educational and fun for children. Purchase Gruyère cheese and Swiss chocolate directly from the farm as authentic souvenirs. Gruyères Castle is an additional CHF 10–12 per adult entry fee. This is a wonderful cultural contrast to the active ski days.

day_by_day.morning: Wake up early for a final Swiss alpine breakfast at the resort. Take a leisurely last walk around the resort grounds or nearby village to soak in the mountain scenery one final time. If time permits, enjoy a short beginner snowshoe walk directly from the resort for a gentle farewell to the Alps.
day_by_day.afternoon: Check out of Aegean Bliss Resort. Depending on departure flight time, stop at a local bakery or café in the village for a final Swiss treat — try a Gipfeli (Swiss croissant) and hot chocolate. Begin transfer to the airport or train station. Browse duty-free shops for Swiss chocolate, watches, and souvenirs at the airport.
day_by_day.evening: Departure from Switzerland. Reflect on an incredible week of skiing, snowshoeing, cultural experiences, and family memories in the Swiss Alps.

meals.breakfast: Final resort breakfast (CHF 18–28 or included). Savor Swiss muesli, fresh bread, local cheeses, and cold cuts one last time.
meals.lunch: Light lunch at a village café or airport restaurant — Swiss-style sandwich, soup, or pastry (CHF 20–30 per person).
meals.dinner: Airport dining or in-flight meal depending on departure time.

day_by_day.notes: Check out time is typically 11:00 — confirm with the resort. Allow at least 3 hours for airport transfer and check-in for international flights. Purchase Swiss chocolate (Lindt, Toblerone, or Läderach) and Gruyère cheese at the airport as final gifts. Ensure all ski rental equipment has been returned by Day 6 or early Day 7 to avoid additional charges. Keep travel documents, lift passes, and receipts organized for the journey home.

highlights: Mix of paid and free experiences

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled — late-night arrival. Flight UA lands at 22:30. Private luxury transfer from airport to Aegean Bliss Resort awaits. Check-in, unwind in your premium suite, and enjoy a welcome amenity prepared by the resort.
day_by_day.afternoon: No activities scheduled — travel day.
day_by_day.evening: Late-night private welcome dinner in-suite or at the resort's exclusive à la carte restaurant. Savor a curated Swiss welcome menu with local cheeses, charcuterie, and warm raclette to ease into the alpine experience.

meals.breakfast: Not applicable (travel day)
meals.lunch: Not applicable (travel day)
meals.dinner: In-suite or resort restaurant welcome dinner — Swiss charcuterie board, raclette, warm fondue, and a selection of fine Swiss wines and hot chocolate for the family

day_by_day.notes: Arrange private airport transfer in advance. Resort concierge should be notified of late arrival to prepare a warm welcome, turn-down service, and light late-night snack basket in the suite. Keep Day 1 restful to prepare for a full Day 2.

day_by_day.morning: Leisurely resort breakfast followed by a private ski fitting and equipment rental session arranged through the resort's ski concierge. Head to the Jungfrau Region Slopes for a guided family ski introduction — enjoy world-class skiing across the interconnected slopes of Grindelwald, Wengen, and Mürren with a certified private ski instructor tailored to all family skill levels.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue skiing on the Jungfrau slopes with your private instructor. Explore the Grindelwald First area with its stunning panoramic runs. Take a mid-afternoon break at a premium mountain-top restaurant for a warm Swiss lunch with views of the Eiger.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort for a spa and wellness session — heated indoor pools, sauna, and alpine herbal treatments. Followed by a fine dining dinner at the resort's signature restaurant.

meals.breakfast: Lavish resort buffet breakfast featuring fresh pastries, Swiss muesli, smoked salmon, artisan cheeses, and freshly squeezed juices
meals.lunch: Lunch at Bergrestaurant Bort or First Cliff Walk restaurant on the mountain — rösti, alpine soup, grilled sausages, and mulled wine for adults, hot chocolate for kids
meals.dinner: Resort signature restaurant — 4-course alpine tasting menu featuring beef tenderloin, truffle risotto, and a Swiss chocolate fondant dessert paired with a curated wine selection

day_by_day.notes: Book private ski instructors at least 48 hours in advance through the resort concierge. Ensure all family members have properly fitted helmets and ski gear. Beginners and young children may prefer the gentler slopes at Grindelwald.

day_by_day.morning: After a hearty breakfast, embark on the iconic Jungfraujoch Top of Europe Train Excursion. Board the cogwheel railway from Grindelwald or Kleine Scheidegg and ascend to 3,454 meters — the highest railway station in Europe. Marvel at the Aletsch Glacier panorama, visit the Ice Palace, and enjoy the Sphinx Observatory viewing platform.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the Jungfraujoch plateau — enjoy snow activities at the top including a family snow disc session and photography at the summit. Descend back by mid-afternoon and explore the charming village of Grindelwald for premium Swiss souvenir shopping and a warm café stop.
day_by_day.evening: Private fondue experience arranged by the resort — either in-suite or at a curated local chalet restaurant in Grindelwald. Traditional Swiss cheese fondue, bread, and charcuterie served fireside with live acoustic alpine music.

meals.breakfast: Resort breakfast — eggs Benedict, freshly baked croissants, Swiss honey, berry compotes, and barista-crafted coffees
meals.lunch: Lunch at the Jungfraujoch Crystal restaurant at the summit — warm soups, sandwiches, and hot beverages with unparalleled glacier views
meals.dinner: Private fondue chalet dinner — classic Gruyère and Emmental cheese fondue, charcuterie platter, roasted potatoes, and a dessert of Swiss meringues with double cream, paired with Fendant white wine

day_by_day.notes: Dress in warm, windproof layers for Jungfraujoch — temperatures at the summit can drop to -15°C or below. The excursion takes approximately 5–6 hours round trip. Book Jungfraujoch tickets in advance to avoid queues. Children under 6 ride free on the railway.

day_by_day.morning: After breakfast, head out for the Glacier Snowshoeing Adventure — a guided family snowshoeing tour across the magnificent Aletsch Glacier, the largest glacier in the Alps. A certified local guide leads the group through pristine snow-covered landscapes with educational commentary on glacier ecology and Swiss alpine heritage.
day_by_day.afternoon: Post-snowshoeing, visit a traditional alpine dairy farm in Gruyères for the Swiss Alpine Cheese and Fondue Cultural Experience. Watch authentic Swiss cheese being made by local artisans, participate in a hands-on cheese tasting workshop, and enjoy a traditional fondue lunch in the rustic farmhouse setting.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort for relaxation. Enjoy a private in-suite family movie night with a curated Swiss dessert spread — hot chocolate, Läderach chocolates, and Swiss pastries — arranged by the butler service.

meals.breakfast: Resort breakfast — full hot buffet with freshly baked breads, alpine cheeses, cold cuts, granola, and seasonal fruit platters
meals.lunch: Gruyères dairy farm — farm-fresh cheese fondue, alpine bread, cured meats, and homemade fruit tarts with farm-produced cream
meals.dinner: In-suite luxury family dining — gourmet Swiss comfort food including veal Zurich-style (Züri Gschnätzlets), buttered spätzle, roasted root vegetables, and a decadent Swiss chocolate mousse

day_by_day.notes: Snowshoeing is suitable for children aged 6 and above. Ensure waterproof boots and warm gloves are worn. The Gruyères dairy farm visit should be pre-booked. Travel between Aletsch and Gruyères requires a private transfer — arrange through the resort concierge for seamless logistics.

day_by_day.morning: After breakfast, enjoy a full morning of freestyle skiing on the Jungfrau Region Slopes — this time explore the Mürren and Wengen sectors for more advanced terrain. Family members with varying skill levels can enjoy separate guided runs before regrouping for a mountain picnic.
day_by_day.afternoon: Experience the Tobogganing on the Fläsch Run — one of Switzerland's most exhilarating natural toboggan runs stretching over 7km from Preda to Bergün. A private transfer takes the family to this legendary run for multiple descents of pure alpine thrill suitable for all ages.
day_by_day.evening: Celebrate a week of adventures with a premium resort gala dinner at the resort's finest dining venue. Dress elegantly for a 5-course chef's tasting menu with wine pairing, followed by a fireside lounge experience with live piano music.

meals.breakfast: Resort champagne breakfast — smoked salmon blinis, eggs royale, artisan pastries, freshly squeezed juices, and premium coffees
meals.lunch: Mountain-top picnic curated by the resort chef — gourmet sandwiches, Swiss cheese selection, charcuterie, warm thermos soups, and chocolate truffles packed in a luxury hamper
meals.dinner: Resort gala dinner — 5-course tasting menu featuring foie gras, lobster bisque, prime Alpine beef fillet, artisan cheese trolley, and a signature Swiss chocolate dessert with wine pairing and non-alcoholic mocktail options for younger guests

day_by_day.notes: The Fläsch toboggan run requires a train ride to Preda — arrange private transfers with the resort. Helmets are recommended and available for rental at the run. The run is open weather permitting; check conditions the morning of. Evening gala dinner reservation should be made 2–3 days in advance with the resort concierge.

day_by_day.morning: A relaxed morning — sleep in and enjoy an extended luxury breakfast at the resort. Afterward, indulge in the resort's premium spa facilities: couples' or family wellness treatments, alpine herb massages, steam rooms, and hydrotherapy pools. A dedicated children's spa program keeps younger guests entertained.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the local alpine village near the resort on a private guided snowshoe walk or horse-drawn sleigh ride through the snowy landscape — a magical and quintessentially Swiss winter experience perfect for families. Stop at a local artisan chocolate shop for a premium Swiss chocolate tasting and personalized chocolate-making workshop.
day_by_day.evening: Private chef's table experience at the resort — a behind-the-scenes culinary journey where the executive chef crafts a personalized menu for the family, with interactive elements for children including making their own Swiss chocolate dessert.

meals.breakfast: Extended resort luxury breakfast — à la carte service including eggs any style, waffles with alpine berry compote, smoked trout, and a full Swiss cold spread
meals.lunch: Light spa lunch at the resort's wellness café — wholesome mountain grain bowls, freshly pressed vegetable juices, warm broths, and artisan herbal teas
meals.dinner: Chef's table private dinner — personalized 6-course menu crafted exclusively for the family, featuring seasonal Swiss ingredients, interactive dessert course, and a curated beverage pairing

day_by_day.notes: Book spa treatments and the chef's table experience at least 2 days in advance. The horse-drawn sleigh ride should be arranged through the concierge and is weather dependent. The chocolate workshop is suitable for children aged 5 and above and makes for a wonderful take-home memory.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in the Swiss Alps — rise early for one last sunrise ski run on the Jungfrau slopes, catching the golden alpenglow over the Eiger, Mönch, and Jungfrau peaks. A truly unforgettable farewell to the mountains. Return to the resort by late morning.
day_by_day.afternoon: Check-out and luggage handling managed seamlessly by the resort's butler service. Enjoy a final leisurely lunch at the resort before your private luxury transfer to the airport. Browse the resort boutique for premium Swiss souvenirs — Läderach chocolates, Swiss watches, and alpine lifestyle gifts.
day_by_day.evening: Private luxury transfer to the airport for departure. Resort concierge arranges fast-track airport assistance. Reflect on an extraordinary week of alpine luxury, world-class skiing, family memories, and Swiss cultural immersion.

meals.breakfast: Farewell resort breakfast — à la carte favorites, fresh pastries, and a commemorative farewell gift of Swiss preserves and chocolates from the resort
meals.lunch: Final resort lunch — Swiss classics including Bündner Gerstensuppe (barley soup), alpine cheese tart, and a light dessert of poached pears with vanilla cream
meals.dinner: Airport lounge or in-flight dining (departure dependent on flight schedule)

day_by_day.notes: Confirm checkout time and departure transfer timing with the concierge the evening before. Allow at least 3 hours before any international flight for transfer and airport procedures from the Swiss Alps region. Request a personalized farewell letter or memory book from the resort — many luxury properties offer this as a complimentary keepsake. Ensure all ski rentals and equipment are returned before checkout.
